deliverables: WP1 - Enabling Onchain Payments & Card Infrastructure
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Bringing Real-World Payments to Cardano with Wirex.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,961,538 ada, consisting of 3,846,153 ada for WP1 and 115,385 ada for an Intersect Budget Administration fee.

Wirex proposes to deliver full-stack, open-source payments infrastructure enabling onchain settlement through smart contracts and connections to banking rails, stablecoin systems, and wallet interfaces.
The proposal states that a core outcome is Visa card issuance linked directly to onchain balances so users can spend digital assets globally at millions of merchants.
Wirex is described as having 7 million users, more than 1.5 million cards issued, more than $20 billion in transaction volume, and experience as a Visa Principal Member.
The proposal asserts that Cardano currently lacks seamless rails for everyday spending, merchant acceptance, and fiat-connected financial activity at scale.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposal asserts that the requested amount does not, at the time of submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
Wirex is stated to have received no ada from the Cardano Treasury within the last 24 months.

Intersect will manage withdrawn funds through a Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract, with specified admin, leadership, and external oversight authorization thresholds.
The document says community auditability will be available through a Sundae treasury dashboard and on-chain verification of the TRSC and PSSC.

summary: The document requests 3,961,538 ada for a Wirex payments infrastructure project, gives a high-level budget and governance custody structure, and makes major adoption and capability claims while omitting detailed milestone, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
